generatedFrom: command-catalog.v1.json plus Contract v1.1 lane proposals, 2026-07-12

commands.name: project.new
commands.nonUndoableReason: Lifecycle action that creates the .mstudio package; there is no prior project state to invert into. Runs through the command bus for uniform UI/MCP/agent access but is not a journal entry.
commands.description: Create a new .mstudio package on disk with an empty timeline. Initial tempo/timeSig/key are set by follow-up project.setTempo/setTimeSig/setKey commands so those mutations are uniformly journaled.

commands.name: project.open
commands.nonUndoableReason: Session action (loads a package into memory); does not mutate project content.
commands.description: Open an existing .mstudio package: read project.json (checkpoint), replay any journal segment newer than the checkpoint, and hydrate the in-memory model.

commands.name: project.save
commands.nonUndoableReason: Checkpoint action, not a content mutation. Its effect is the project.json-checkpoint-plus-journal-truncation-marker sequence described in 02-ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, which is orthogonal to the per-edit journal this schema validates.
commands.description: Write project.json as a checkpoint of the current journal tip and mark prior journal segments eligible for truncation once the write is durable.

commands.name: project.setTempo
commands.description: Set the project's global tempo in beats per minute. v1 has one tempo for the whole project (no tempo map / tempo automation).

commands.name: project.setTimeSig
commands.description: Set the project's global time signature, e.g. 4/4 or 6/8.

commands.name: project.setKey

key.description: Matches the keyscale vocabulary already used by ace_generator.py (e.g. 'C major', 'A minor').

commands.description: Set the project's key/scale metadata (informational for v1; not enforced against note content).

commands.name: section.set
commands.description: Create or update a named arrangement section marker. Catalog default inverse is section.remove (correct for the create case); when section.set updates an EXISTING sectionId's fields, the runtime executor uses a self-inverse (section.set with the prior name/startTicks/color) instead. See engine/contracts/README.md open question: this is an upsert command with a context-dependent inverse, which a static per-command inverseRule cannot fully express.

commands.name: section.remove
commands.description: Remove an arrangement section marker.

commands.name: marker.set
commands.description: Create or update a timeline marker. Catalog default inverse is marker.remove (correct for the create case; P0-C proposal 1, APPROVED by the coordinating session 2026-07-11, mirroring section.set/section.remove); when marker.set updates an EXISTING markerId's fields, the runtime executor uses a self-inverse (marker.set with the prior positionTicks/label/color) instead, the same upsert nuance as section.set.

commands.name: marker.remove
commands.description: Remove a timeline marker. Added as marker.set's undo-completing counterpart (P0-C proposal 1, APPROVED by the coordinating session 2026-07-11), mirroring section.remove.

commands.name: transport.play
commands.description: Start playback from the current transport position. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4: transport commands are real commands on the bus but never appear in journal.jsonl.

commands.name: transport.stop
commands.description: Stop playback.

commands.name: transport.seek
commands.description: Move the transport playhead to an absolute tick position.

commands.name: transport.loop.set
commands.description: Set the transport loop region.

commands.name: transport.loop.clear
commands.description: Clear the transport loop region.

commands.name: transport.metronome
commands.description: Toggle the metronome click. v1 metronome is a simple click, no accent patterns or sound choices.

commands.name: track.add
commands.description: Add a new track. index is optional (append if omitted).

commands.name: track.remove
commands.description: Remove a track and every clip placed on it.

commands.name: track.rename
commands.description: Rename a track.

commands.name: track.reorder
commands.description: Move a track to a new position in the track list.

commands.name: track.setColor
commands.description: Set a track's display color.

commands.name: track.setHeight
commands.description: Set a track's lane height in the timeline canvas.

commands.name: track.mute
commands.description: Mute or unmute a track.

commands.name: track.solo
commands.description: Solo or unsolo a track.

commands.name: track.arm
commands.description: Arm or disarm a track for recording. The armed track is the capture target for record.start; arming is journaled and undoable.

commands.name: record.start

trackId.description: The armed track to capture onto.

deviceId.description: Input device name to open; the system default input device when omitted.

startTicks.description: Where the captured clip lands (bar-snapped by the host). Default: the transport position, or 0.

punchOutTicks.description: Punch-out position. When set, record.stop lands a clip of exactly punchOutTicks minus startTicks (the punch region), truncating or silence-padding the capture to fit. Omitted means open-ended capture until record.stop.

commands.description: Begin capturing from an audio input onto an armed track. Opens an INPUT-only stream and never an output stream; monitoring stays silent unless separately gated by MAJIKS_TEST_AUDIBLE. With punchOutTicks set, the capture auto-fits the punch region. Unjournaled transport-class action: the take and clip landed by record.stop are the journaled, undoable unit. Ships with the L19 recording lane.

commands.name: record.rotate
commands.description: Complete the current loop-record pass without stopping or reopening the input stream. The host rotates the writer-side capture accumulator, immediately continues filling the next pass, and prepares the completed pass asynchronously before committing its atomic record transaction. No-op when nothing is recording.

commands.name: record.stop
commands.description: Stop the active capture and land the recorded audio as a candidate take and a placed clip with human-origin lineage (txn.begin / gen.landed sourceCommand record.commit / clip.place / txn.commit). No-op when nothing is recording.

commands.name: record.cancel
commands.description: Discard the active capture without landing a take or clip. No-op when nothing is recording.

commands.name: midi.device.select

device.description: Reported port name, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

map.description: A map key (file stem or map name), 'none' to leave the port unmapped, or 'auto' to return to pattern auto-detect.

commands.description: Pin or unpin the map for a MIDI input port.

commands.name: midi.learn.start

device.description: Scope capture to one port name. Omitted: first control from any device.

commands.description: Open the MIDI learn session.

commands.name: midi.learn.stop
commands.description: Close the MIDI learn session.

commands.name: midi.binding.set

device.description: Port name whose resolved map takes the binding. Default: the learn session's captured device.

number.description: Note or CC number. Omitted for pitchBend (channel-wide).

control.description: Explicit control coordinates. Default: the learn session's captured control.

name.description: kind=command: a catalog command name. kind=builtin: one of the built-in action names.

params.description: kind=command: the params template, may contain '$value' and '$track:N' placeholders.

instruction.description: kind=sterling: the instruction text queued for Sterling.

commands.description: Create or replace one MIDI binding and persist it.

commands.name: midi.binding.clear
commands.description: Remove one MIDI binding from a device's user overlay map.

commands.name: midi.map.import

overwrite.description: Replace an existing user map with the same file name.

commands.description: Copy an external MIDI map file into the user maps directory.

commands.name: midi.map.export

map.description: Map key (file stem or map name).

commands.description: Write a MIDI map file body verbatim to a path outside the app directory.

commands.name: midi.reload
commands.description: Re-read bundled and user MIDI maps from disk and re-resolve connected ports.

commands.name: clip.place

assetHash.description: blake3 of the audio asset under audio/, per section 6.

commands.description: Place a clip referencing a content-addressed audio asset onto a track at a given position.

commands.name: clip.move

trackId.description: Destination track; equal to the clip's current track for a same-lane move.

commands.description: Move a clip to a new start position, optionally onto a different track. This is the exact command shown as the worked example in 02-ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.

commands.name: clip.trim

deltaTicks.description: Signed; positive shortens from the start edge or lengthens from the end edge.

commands.description: Trim a clip's start or end edge.

commands.name: clip.split

newClipId.description: Id assigned to the right-hand piece created by the split.

commands.description: Split a clip into two clips at a tick position.

commands.name: clip.duplicate
commands.description: Duplicate a clip onto the same or another track at a given position.

commands.name: clip.remove
commands.description: Remove a clip from the timeline. The underlying audio asset is not deleted (content-addressed, may be referenced elsewhere).

commands.name: clip.setGain
commands.description: Set a clip's gain trim, independent of the track's mixer gain.

commands.name: clip.mute
commands.description: Mute or unmute an individual clip.

commands.name: clip.fade.set

lengthTicks.description: Not named explicitly in 02-ARCH section 4's one-line description (in/out, shape); required for the command to be executable, added here.

commands.description: Set a clip's fade-in or fade-out.

commands.name: clip.crossfade.set
commands.description: Set a crossfade between two adjacent clips on the same track.

commands.name: clip.warp.set

stretchRatio.description: Required when mode is 'ratio'; 1.0 is unwarped.

commands.description: Set a clip's time-warp: a fixed stretch ratio, or conform to the project tempo.

commands.name: clip.phaseAnchor.set

anchorTicks.description: Timeline bar-grid phase anchor for the clip's warped source.

commands.description: Set the timeline phase anchor used when a warped clip is locked to the bar grid.

commands.name: clip.rename
commands.description: Rename a clip's display label.

commands.name: autolane.show
commands.nonUndoableReason: View-state toggle (whether an automation lane is expanded under a track), not a content mutation.
commands.description: Show or hide an automation lane in the timeline UI.

commands.name: autopoint.add
commands.description: Add an automation point on a track parameter lane. v1 automation targets are track.volume and track.pan only.

commands.name: autopoint.move
commands.description: Move an existing automation point to a new position and/or value.

commands.name: autopoint.remove
commands.description: Remove an automation point.

commands.name: autolane.clear
commands.description: Remove every automation point on a lane. Undo restores the full prior point set (runtime snapshot, not expressed field-by-field in this schema).

commands.name: mix.gain
commands.description: Set a track's mixer channel gain (distinct from clip.setGain, which trims an individual clip).

commands.name: mix.pan
commands.description: Set a track's mixer pan, -1 (full left) to 1 (full right).

commands.name: mix.eq
commands.description: Set one band of a track's channel EQ.

commands.name: mix.send
commands.description: Set a track's send level to bus A or bus B.

commands.name: mix.master.gain
commands.description: Set the master bus gain.

commands.name: mix.limiter.set
commands.description: Enable/disable and configure the master limiter. mute/solo are on track.mute/track.solo, not here.

request.description: Full shape is the Gen Protocol 'generate' request (gen-protocol.v1.yaml); see gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.description: Request a new text2music generation and stage it as a take. Gen Protocol op: generate.

commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

scope.description: One scope name or an array of stem names. all-stems is only valid as a scalar; arrays select multiple stems and null-preserve the rest.

request.description: Full shape is the Gen Protocol 'revise' request; see gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.description: Request a region repaint with an instruction delta and stage the result as a take. Gen Protocol op: revise.

commands.name: gen.extend
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

request.description: Full shape is the Gen Protocol 'extend' request; see gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.description: Request that a clip's audio be continued by addedDurationSeconds and stage the result as a take. Gen Protocol op: extend.

commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

request.description: Full shape is the Gen Protocol 'layer' request; see gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.description: Request a new stem that fits harmonically/rhythmically with existing context audio (lego mode). Gen Protocol op: layer.

commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

commands.description: Request a fresh-seed variation of an existing region or whole-song take, same prompt. Gen Protocol op: retake.

commands.name: gen.autocomplete
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

request.description: Full shape is the Gen Protocol 'autocomplete' request; see gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

commands.name: gen.separate
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

engine.description: demucs: htdemucs 4-stem separation (default separator). ace-extract: ACE-Step generative extraction, labeled generative in lineage, per 02-ARCH section 5.

commands.description: Request stem separation of a clip. Gen Protocol op: separate.

commands.name: gen.cancel
commands.nonUndoableReason: Cancellation is not itself invertible.
commands.description: Cancel an in-flight gen request. KNOWN v1 BACKEND GAP (see gen-protocol-mapping.md): the current Python backend's cancel_generation RPC is a single global cancel flag, not per-job; the Gen Protocol's per-requestId cancel is the target contract, not yet the shipped behavior.

commands.name: gen.finalize
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async re-render REQUEST only; the resulting swap is applied when gen.landed arrives.

draftTakeId.description: The committed draft take being re-rendered at higher quality.

targetQualityRung.description: draft=acestep-v15-turbo (8 steps), standard=acestep-v15-quality (step count not yet observed in any shipped call site, see gen-protocol-mapping.md open question), full=acestep-v15-base (50 steps). finalize always targets a rung higher than the draft's own rung.

request.description: Same request shape as the revise op that produced draftTakeId (identical region + instruction + scope); only the model/steps rung changes. See gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.description: Re-render a committed draft take at full quality and splice it in place: same region, same lineage, journaled as a swap. This is the draft/commit re-render swap named in 02-ARCH section 4's gen catalog line.

commands.name: gen.landed
commands.nonUndoableReason: System-authored completion record of an async gen.* request; not itself a user-invocable command.

requestId.description: Matches the requestId of the gen.* command that started this job.

assetHashes.description: Keys are 'mix' for a single-file take or stem names (vocals/drums/bass/other) for a per-stem take.

commands.description: Written by the engine (actor.kind=system) when any async gen.* request reaches a terminal success state. Carries the provenance the lineage tree and export manifests read: asset hashes + engine identity, per 02-ARCH section 4 ('completion journals gen.landed with asset hashes') and section 5 ('terminal ... with artifact paths + content hashes + engine identity for lineage').

commands.name: take.promote

targetClipId.description: Clip the take is spliced into; for a new gen.song this may be a clip created as part of promotion.

commands.description: Commit a generated take into the timeline, splicing it into (or creating) a clip. This is the undoable step that actually mutates the visible project; the gen.* request that produced the take is not itself undoable.

commands.name: take.discard
commands.description: Discard a generated take. The take's asset stays under takes/ until the user purges it (section 6); discard only removes it from the active candidate list, so it remains reversible.

commands.name: take.purge
commands.description: Mark an un-promoted candidate take offline so its unreferenced audio may be reclaimed. The journaled state change preserves lineage and is undoable.

commands.name: take.restore
commands.description: Restore an offline candidate take's journal state after undoing take.purge. Audio reclamation is host-managed and may require regeneration or recovery before audition.

commands.name: take.auditionMix
commands.nonUndoableReason: Preview/listening action (which per-stem take is heard while auditioning), not a committed mutation.
commands.description: Select which stems of a per-stem take are audible while auditioning candidates, without committing anything.

commands.name: import.audio

separate.description: Run htdemucs on import and place stems as separate tracks.

conform.description: Time-stretch the imported audio to the project tempo on import.

commands.description: Import an external audio file, copy it content-addressed into audio/, and place it as a clip.

commands.name: import.stems
commands.description: Import a directory of audio stems as aligned tracks, copied content-addressed into audio/.

commands.name: export.master
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes a file outside the project package; it does not mutate project content. Per 02-ARCH section 4's acceptance hook, export.* is journaled (provenance: what was exported, when, from which state) but explicitly non-undoable, same as transport.

loudnessTarget.description: Normalize the master to an EBU R128 integrated-LUFS target (streaming -14, club -7, broadcast -16). Omitted or 'none' writes the mix as bounced.

includeManifest.description: Also write the AI-disclosure provenance manifest next to the audio (<output>.manifest.json).

commands.description: Bounce the full master mix to a file, via the render graph's offline path (same graph as realtime, per 02-ARCH section 3). WAV is 24-bit at the project rate; AAC via Apple AudioToolbox. Optional loudness target + provenance manifest (L13).

commands.name: export.stems
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes files outside the project package; see export.master.

includeManifest.description: Also write the AI-disclosure provenance manifest next to the stems (stems.manifest.json).

commands.description: Bounce per-track or per-stem stems to files (24-bit WAV; not loudness-normalized). Optional provenance manifest (L13).

commands.name: export.region
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes a file outside the project package; see export.master.

loudnessTarget.description: Normalize the region to an EBU R128 integrated-LUFS target. Omitted or 'none' writes the region as bounced.

includeManifest.description: Also write the AI-disclosure provenance manifest next to the audio (<output>.manifest.json).

commands.description: Bounce a time region of the master mix to a file (24-bit WAV or AAC). Optional loudness target + provenance manifest (L13).

commands.name: export.manifest
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes a file outside the project package; see export.master.
commands.description: Write the provenance manifest (rebuildable view over the journal, per section 6) to a standalone file.

commands.name: publish.track
commands.nonUndoableReason: Publishes to majiks.online, an external system; not a local project mutation.
commands.description: Publish an exported asset with provenance cert via the existing majiks.online publish path (shipped pre-Studio; params kept minimal here since the pipeline itself is out of this program's scope).

commands.name: txn.begin
commands.nonUndoableReason: Structural bracket marker, not a content mutation itself. Atomicity applies to the journaled commands between this and the matching txn.commit (02-ARCH section 4: 'Multi-op user gestures wrap in txn.begin/txn.commit (atomic undo unit)'); undoing the group is driven by walking that bracketed range, not by inverting txn.begin directly.
commands.description: Open an atomic transaction: journaled commands until the matching txn.commit undo/redo as one unit. v1 transactions do not nest (one open txnId at a time).

commands.name: txn.commit
commands.nonUndoableReason: Structural bracket marker; see txn.begin.
commands.description: Close the atomic transaction opened by the txn.begin with the same txnId. Conformance checks that every txn.commit has a preceding, matching, not-yet-closed txn.begin.

commands.name: studio.importStemSession
commands.description: Bring an existing Stem Sessions multitrack session onto the Studio timeline as tracks+clips. Flag v1.1; Stem Sessions itself stays untouched (02-ARCH section 1).
